mechanism_narrative: A positive quarterly growth rate in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates expanding economic activity, which increases corporate earnings expectations and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where GDPC1 growth rate is positive over the prior quarter.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) falls below 0.2%, it signals an accommodative monetary policy environment that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS < 0.2% in the prior month but SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and decreases in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicate a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS increase and UNRATE decrease occur but SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.5% YoY), the Federal Reserve's response of raising interest rates (FEDFUNDS > 1.0%) leads to a contraction in equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.5% indicates rising economic output, which supports corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO change > 0.5% but SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer confidence and construction activity, which correlates with higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST increases but SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.15% over the prior month signals immediate monetary easing, which typically results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS < 0.15% but SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly growth in real GDP (GDPC1) exceeding 2.0% indicates robust economic expansion, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth > 2.0% but SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.
